peer_compute_note: X1 -> X2 is a two-variable comparison: X2 sets DSV4_CUDA_PEER_DEVICE=1 and DSV4_CUDA_PEER_COMPUTE=0, while X1 sets neither (no X1 engine_environ.txt has DSV4_CUDA_PEER_COMPUTE). Code inspection at d0e19de2 says the second variable is inert in X1: DSV4_CUDA_PEER_COMPUTE is read only inside peer_runs() (c/backend_cuda_dsv4.cu:1410-1412), which is called only for an expert mirrored on another device (backend_cuda_dsv4.cu:2107) and, through dsv4_cuda_peer_compute(), from v4_peer_mirrors_create (c/deepseek_v4.c:11812); neither path exists without DSV4_CUDA_PEER_DEVICE. So X1 -> X2 very likely measures the p2p-read peer pool alone, but that rests on reading the code, not on a measured X1 + DSV4_CUDA_PEER_COMPUTE=0 arm. It is therefore kept as a supplementary record (supplementary/pr2-peer-device-p2p-read-two-variable.json, changed_variables names both; c/experiment_manifest.py rejects it by design), and the strictly one-variable records for the peer pool are pr2-peer-device-compute.json (X1 -> X3) and pr2-peer-compute.json (X2 -> X3). To make X1 -> X2 strict, measure an X1 + DSV4_CUDA_PEER_COMPUTE=0 arm (3 samples) in a later GPU window.

notes.manifest_set: Lead PR #2 with the strictly one-variable records pr2-peer-device-compute.json (X1 -> X3, 1.374x) and pr2-peer-compute.json (X2 -> X3, 1.175x), with pr2-resident-first.json (G1 -> X1, 1.027x) for the one-GPU step. X1 -> X2 (p2p-read peer pool, 1.169x) changes two variables, so it is kept only as the supplementary record supplementary/pr2-peer-device-p2p-read-two-variable.json, which c/experiment_manifest.py rejects by design; see peer_compute_note.

vs_earlier_single_sample.text: Medians are 3.1-4.5% above the earlier single-sample numbers (G1 2.78 -> 2.8660, +3.1%, X1 2.84 -> 2.9432, +3.6%, X2 3.32 -> 3.4405, +3.6%, X3 3.87 -> 4.0438, +4.5%). Likely cause, not tested in this run: the earlier runs had COLI_CUDA_MOE_DOUBLE=1 set (review F43; the review measured the double bank costing about 3-5% of decode) and used intermediate PR #2 binaries; this run isolated neither factor.

notes.cache_state: The OS page cache was not dropped between samples, and round 1 was partly cold: the serve unit's systemd memory peak was 14.3G for X1/s1 (seq 2) and 7.6G for X2/s1 (seq 3) and X3/s1 (seq 4), against 7.3G for every other sample (10 of 13, including G1/s1, seq 1). That is consistent with those servers reading model pages that were not cached yet; they are not systematically slower (X1/s1 -0.07%, X2/s1 +0.03%, X3/s1 +0.00% vs their arm medians).
